draft.title: Comparing before you buy
card: A smart consumer compares prices and quality at more than one shop before buying. The cheapest item is not always the best choice if it breaks quickly.
Unit pricing shows the cost per standard amount, such as per 100 grams or per litre. It lets you compare packs of different sizes fairly.
Reviews from other buyers can show how a product works in real life. Read several, because one review may not be typical.
Check the full cost, not just the sticker price. Delivery fees, booking fees and extra charges can make a cheap offer cost more.
draft.remember: Compare price, quality, unit price, reviews and the full cost before you pay.

a.q: Why is unit pricing useful when comparing a small and a large pack of pasta?
opts: It shows the cost per 100 grams for both packs
It shows which pack has the better brand name
It shows which pack other buyers reviewed best
It shows which pack has no delivery fee added
a.why: Unit pricing gives the cost for the same amount, so the two packs can be compared fairly. Reviews are a different tool, and they do not tell you the cost per amount.
a.clue: Think about what is the same for both packs.

b.q: Ravi finds a skateboard for $60 on a website. Another site sells it for $68 with free delivery. The first site adds $12 delivery. Which site is cheaper, and why?
opts: The second site, because its full cost is $68
The first site, because its sticker price is $60
The second site, because free delivery is always best
The first site, because delivery fees are not a cost
b.why: The first site costs $60 plus $12, which is $72 in total. The second site costs $68, so it is cheaper. The $60 sticker price is tempting, but it leaves out the delivery fee.

a.best: It shows the cost per 100 grams for both packs

b.best: The second site, because its full cost is $68
